blockers.problem: The frozen rule requires >= 1200 usable sentences per document. The K=3 candidate pools are institutional landing pages and index pages, not long-form documents; batch-6 Wikipedia articles yielded only 150-350 usable sentences after cleaning.
blockers.consequence: With the threshold as frozen, no domain is likely to qualify, and the rule would degrade into a documented shortfall across all 12 domains rather than a corpus.
blockers.not_done: The threshold was NOT lowered silently. That would be a post-hoc change to a frozen selection rule.

blockers.problem: Search results include social media and commercial blogs (facebook.com, linkedin.com, tandfonline, samlog blog, energyinnovation.org, epi.org, stibosystems.com).
blockers.handling: Mechanical allowlist filter applies before K=3 selection, so these are excluded without analyst judgement; recorded here as a mechanical filter step, not a discretionary choice.

blockers.problem: Many top-ranked results are navigation/landing pages whose content is tables, links and boilerplate rather than prose.
blockers.consequence: Section-wise sampling presupposes real sections; landing pages would yield almost no qualifying sentences.

blockers.problem: The frozen >=3 real sections criterion is measured by counting markdown '##' headings. The PDF parser returns flat text, so long and genuinely sectioned PDFs are scored sections=1 and rejected, while HTML pages with proper heading markup pass.
blockers.evidence: WHO Technical Report Series No. 957: 2365 usable sentences - by far the richest document seen so far - rejected solely on sections=1.
blockers.consequence: Continuing the fetch as-is would systematically bias the corpus toward HTML documents with heading markup and away from long-form PDFs. That is a silent selection artifact and would distort exactly the corpus this replication test depends on.
blockers.not_done: The section counter was NOT loosened and no fallback section detection was added. Either would be a post-hoc change to a frozen qualification criterion and must come as a new frozen rule version.
decision_required: new frozen rule version with format-robust section detection
or change the corpus unit back to HTML long-form documents
or accept the bias knowingly and document it as a limitation
Keep 1200 and accept 12 documented shortfalls (no corpus)?
Lower the per-document minimum to a feasible value (rule change: requires a new frozen version of batch7_source_selection_v1)?
Change the fetch target type to long-form documents (e.g. full PDF reports) and keep the threshold (rule change: same requirement)?
